samples.summary: New Cmd+Shift+V guard tests assert only negatives, with no positive control that the clipboard path ever ran
samples.evidence: Both new tests ('a plain-text paste whose clipboard read resolves during the yield is refused', line ~401, and '...resolves after dispose writes nothing', line ~430) only assert that 'PLAIN' is absent / text is still 'seed'. Nothing asserts the stubbed `readText` was called or that a plain-text paste *does* land when the guards are not tripped. `installPendingClipboard()` returns a `release`, but the returned readText spy is never asserted on. If `dispatchPastePlain`'s modifier combo, the `mod && shiftKey` branch (text-editor.ts:1373), or the clipboard stub install ever stop reaching `pastePlainTextFromClipboard()`, both tests still pass green — they are exactly the shape of a guard test that cannot fail. The only positive control for this shortcut lives in a different package/file (frontend editor-undo-selection.test.ts), so this file's coverage of the new `if (this.disposed || this.pasting) return;` guard (text-editor.ts:4254) is unverified within its own setup.

samples.summary: New `requestLayoutRefresh` seam (measure-without-paint during an open undo unit) has no test at all
samples.evidence: `textEditor.requestLayoutRefresh = recomputeLayout` (editor.ts:2531) and the wrapper that calls it while `undoUnitDepth > 0` (text-editor.ts:736-740) are the mechanism that keeps `getLayout()` (blockParentMap / `getCellInfo` / wrap affinity) fresh inside a held-render unit. Grep for `requestLayoutRefresh` across the repo finds only src files and design/task docs — no test file references it, and no new test exercises a composite action (e.g. paste or Enter over a selection inside a table cell) whose branch depends on a refreshed layout mid-unit. The frontend paint-count test only asserts `ctxCalls.save === 1`, which passes whether or not the layout was recomputed. If the assignment were dropped, nothing in the suite would fail, yet the paste path branching on stale `blockParentMap` would put content in the wrong place.

samples.summary: Hangul commit-over-a-selection now wrapped in `withUndoUnit`, but no test covers the selection-replacement Hangul path
samples.evidence: `applyHangulResult` wraps `deleteSelection()` + `docInsertText()` in `withUndoUnit` (text-editor.ts:5891). This is the same #1045 shape (delete N blocks, then write) for Korean typing over a select-all, so losing the unit reproduces the same unrecoverable-tail data loss the diff exists to fix. hangul.test.ts only exercises `HangulAssembler` directly (no editor, no selection); ime-composition-editor.test.ts documents that it cannot assert Yorkie undo-unit counts; text-box-composing.test.ts is the slides text-box preview. No test in docs or frontend types a jamo over a non-empty selection and counts undo units.

samples.summary: `withUndoUnit`'s documented throw behavior (depth unwound, held render still replayed) is untested
samples.evidence: The doc comment claims interior renders are replayed 'at most once — after the outermost unit commits, including after a throw' (text-editor.ts:3820-3830) and the `finally` block implements it (3843-3849). No test throws from inside a `withUndoUnit`/`doc.batch` body to check that `undoUnitDepth` returns to 0 and the pending paint fires; a leaked depth would silently suppress every later render. Searched the new frontend and docs tests for a throwing body — the only throw-related batch test is MemDocStore-level ('setDocument() inside a batch throws'), which does not go through `withUndoUnit`.
searchedFor: grep withUndoUnit in packages/frontend/tests and packages/docs/test

samples.summary: Programmatic `insertText()` (slides type-to-edit entry) newly wrapped in `withUndoUnit` — no test for its one-unit / render-hold behavior
samples.evidence: `TextEditor.insertText()` (text-editor.ts:828-845) now batches delete+insert. Grepping packages/slides/test for `insertText(` finds no callers, and no docs test asserts that a programmatic insert over a selection costs one undo unit or that the held render is replayed. Failure would be a second dead Cmd+Z in slides text boxes rather than data loss, hence minor.

samples.summary: The `handleBackspace` shape (snapshot, empty deleteSelection unit, then writes) is only pinned at store level, not through the editor
samples.evidence: MemDocStore's 'an adopted checkpoint survives a batch that writes nothing' (packages/docs/test/store/memory.test.ts:467) simulates the shape with `store.snapshot(); store.batch(() => {}); store.deleteText(...)`, but no editor-level test presses Backspace with a *collapsed* caret and then undoes, which is the real path now that `deleteSelection()` always opens a batch (text-editor.ts:3863). The frontend suite only covers backspace over a select-all. If the adoption rule regressed, a plain backspace would become unundoable and only the store-level unit test would catch it.

finding.summary: New Cmd+Shift+V guard tests assert only negatives, with no positive control that the clipboard path ever ran
finding.evidence: Both new tests ('a plain-text paste whose clipboard read resolves during the yield is refused', line ~401, and '...resolves after dispose writes nothing', line ~430) only assert that 'PLAIN' is absent / text is still 'seed'. Nothing asserts the stubbed `readText` was called or that a plain-text paste *does* land when the guards are not tripped. `installPendingClipboard()` returns a `release`, but the returned readText spy is never asserted on. If `dispatchPastePlain`'s modifier combo, the `mod && shiftKey` branch (text-editor.ts:1373), or the clipboard stub install ever stop reaching `pastePlainTextFromClipboard()`, both tests still pass green — they are exactly the shape of a guard test that cannot fail. The only positive control for this shortcut lives in a different package/file (frontend editor-undo-selection.test.ts), so this file's coverage of the new `if (this.disposed || this.pasting) return;` guard (text-editor.ts:4254) is unverified within its own setup.

verdict.reason: The finding's core claim — that both new tests "still pass green" and "cannot fail" — is contradicted by the code. Removing the guard under test (text-editor.ts:4254 `if (this.disposed || this.pasting) return;`) makes both tests fail: in test 1 (large-paste-indicator.test.ts:402-428) the released read would run `insertPlainText('PLAIN')` while `pasting` is true, and the deferred large paste only *inserts* blocks (text-editor.ts:1555-1569, deferPaste 1604-1622), so `'PLAIN'` survives and `expect(text).not.toContain('PLAIN')` fails; in test 2 (435-454) `dispose()` (text-editor.ts:6061-6087) only detaches listeners and leaves doc/store writable, so without the `disposed` check the write lands and `expect(text).toBe('seed')` fails. The reachability drift the finding hypothesizes is separately pinned by a positive control in the same repo suite: packages/frontend/tests/app/docs/editor-undo-selection.test.ts:432-470 drives the identical Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+V combo against the same @wafflebase/docs editor with the same defineProperty clipboard stub and asserts `readText` was called and the plain text landed (`texts()` === ['Pasted']). The harness is also demonstrably wired: both ctrlKey and metaKey are set so `mod` is true on either platform (text-editor.ts:1085-1088) and hits `mod && shiftKey → pastePlainTextFromClipboard()` (1373-1376). What is left is a hygiene wish for an in-file positive control, not vacuous coverage, a missing test for the changed behavior, or over-mocking (only the browser clipboard boundary is stubbed) — not blocking under the test-adequacy rubric. The finding also misdescribes the helper: installPendingClipboard (137-157) returns `{release, restore}`, no readText spy exists to assert on.

mergedFrom.summary: Programmatic `insertText()` (slides type-to-edit entry) newly wrapped in `withUndoUnit` — no test for its one-unit / render-hold behavior
mergedFrom.evidence: `TextEditor.insertText()` (text-editor.ts:828-845) now batches delete+insert. Grepping packages/slides/test for `insertText(` finds no callers, and no docs test asserts that a programmatic insert over a selection costs one undo unit or that the held render is replayed. Failure would be a second dead Cmd+Z in slides text boxes rather than data loss, hence minor.

verdict.reason: The claimed code is real: text-editor.ts:5891-5894 wraps deleteSelection() + docInsertText() in withUndoUnit inside applyHangulResult's commit branch, and the task doc (20260907-docs-select-all-type-undo-todo.md:34-37) names "the Hangul commit path" as part of this change. I searched repo-wide for any test that drives a jamo through the editor over a non-empty selection and/or counts undo units: all files containing Hangul characters (ts/tsx/js/mjs/spec/md/json), all tests using getUndoStackForTest/undo(), the docs, frontend and slides test trees, and the browser smoke script. The only editor-level Hangul tests (ime-composition-editor.test.ts:167-176, text-box-composing.test.ts:54-137) run on an empty block with no selection and assert only committed text — ime-composition-editor.test.ts:19-22 says outright it cannot assert Yorkie undo-unit counts. editor-undo-selection.test.ts covers ASCII typing, backspace, Enter, page break and both paste flavors over a select-all but contains no jamo at all. No e2e suite exists and verify-ime-browser.mjs has no select/undo. So the selection-replacement Hangul path has no meaningful coverage; if its unit is dropped, a Korean user typing over a select-all on a >50-block document loses the document tail permanently — the exact defect the diff exists to prevent. Major, blocking under the test-adequacy rubric.
